title: A film you recommended
goal: Choose between -(y)An and -DIk, talk about books and films you liked, and follow a message recommending a film.

intro.text: One question decides: is the noun the subject of the verb? Yes: `-(y)An` (*beni gören adam*, the man who saw me). No: `-DIk` with a possessive (*gördüğüm adam*, the man I saw).

exercises.title: Bir film önerisi
exercises.passage:
Selam Can,

Geçen hafta bana önerdiğin filmi sonunda izledim. Çok beğendim! Film, İstanbul'da yaşayan yaşlı bir şairin hikâyesini anlatıyor. Şairin yazdığı son şiir, filmin de adı. En sevdiğim sahne, şairin çocukluğunun geçtiği köye döndüğü sahne. Filmdeki oyuncuların hepsi çok iyiydi, ama şairi oynayan oyuncu harikaydı.

Anlamadığım tek bir şey var: filmin sonu. Şair köyde mi kalıyor, İstanbul'a mı dönüyor? Sen ne düşünüyorsun? Bir de, bu hafta sonu izleyeceğimiz filmi sen seç.

Görüşürüz,

Elif

glossary.en: to spend one's childhood (literally: one's childhood passes)

exercises.translation: Hi Can, Last week you recommended a film to me, and I've finally watched it. I liked it a lot! The film tells the story of an old poet who lives in Istanbul. The last poem the poet wrote is also the title of the film. My favourite scene is the one where the poet goes back to the village where he spent his childhood. All the actors in the film were very good, but the actor who played the poet was wonderful. There's just one thing I didn't understand: the end of the film. Does the poet stay in the village, or does he go back to Istanbul? What do you think? And you choose the film we'll watch this weekend. See you, Elif

questions.explain: *Bana önerdiğin film*: **the film you recommended to me**, and Elif is writing to Can.

options: An old poet who lives in Istanbul
A young actor in a village
questions.explain: *İstanbul'da yaşayan yaşlı bir şair*: `-(y)An`, the poet is the one who lives there.

questions.q: Which scene did Elif like best?
options: The poet going back to the village of his childhood
The poet writing his last poem

questions.q: What does Elif ask Can to do?
options: Choose the film for the weekend
questions.explain: *Bu hafta sonu izleyeceğimiz filmi sen seç*: `-(y)AcAk` + *-imiz*, **the film we'll watch**.

exercises.question: Which means **the man who saw me**?

why.1: *Gördüğüm adam* is **the man I saw**: you did the seeing.
why.2: With *beni* as the object, the man must be the subject, so `-(y)An`: *beni gören adam*.

exercises.explain: The man did the seeing, so he is the subject: `-(y)An`, *gören*.

exercises.text: Bu kelimenin anlamını bil___ biri var mı?
exercises.en: Is there anyone who knows the meaning of this word?
exercises.explain: The person does the knowing: subject, so `-(y)An`, *bilen biri*.

exercises.text: Şairin yaz___ son şiir çok ünlü.
exercises.en: The last poem the poet wrote is very famous.

reject.why: The poem didn't write: the poet did. The poem is the object, so `-DIk`: *yazdığı*.

exercises.explain: *şairin yaz-dığ-ı*: the poet in the genitive, `-DIk` + *-ı*.

exercises.en: The actor who played the poet was very good.

exercises.prompt: Anlamadığım tek bir şey var: filmin sonu.
accept: There is only one thing I do not understand: the end of the film.
There is just one thing I [do not understand|did not understand]: the [end|ending] of the [film|movie].
There is only one thing I did not understand: the [end|ending] of the [film|movie].
There is only one thing I do not understand: the [ending of the film|end of the movie|ending of the movie].

exercises.prompt: You choose the film we will watch this weekend.
exercises.text: Bu hafta sonu izleyeceğimiz filmi sen seç.
accept: Bu hafta sonu izleyeceğimiz filmi siz seçin.

exercises.en: Is there anyone who knows me?

exercises.explain: You do the loving and the people are the object: `-DIk` + *-in* (your), *sev-diğ-in*. *Seni seven insanlar* would be the people who love you.

exercises.prompt: I know the man who lives in this house.

reject.why: The man does the living here: he is the subject, so `-(y)An`, *oturan adam*.

exercises.prompt: Did you see the house he lives in?

reject.why: The house doesn't live anywhere: he lives in it. Use `-DIk`: *oturduğu ev*.
